title: City Mayor
description: You have just been elected mayor of a rapidly growing Indian city. Juggle budget pressures, a public health crisis, and powerful competing interests — every decision you make affects real lives.
learning_objectives: Understand the trade-offs inherent in public resource allocation
Practice ethical decision-making when powerful interests conflict with public good
Develop strategic thinking for managing multiple stakeholders simultaneously
Build empathy for the full spectrum of a community's needs, not just the loudest voices
Recognise how short-term decisions create long-term systemic outcomes
learning_concept: Governance is the art of making decisions under uncertainty with incomplete information — knowing that inaction is itself a choice with consequences.
psychological_framework: Public Value Theory (Moore) — creating value for citizens beyond economic efficiency, balancing legitimacy, capacity, and stakeholder authorisation

glossary_terms.definition: A benefit that is available to all citizens and cannot be withheld from any individual, such as clean air or public parks.
The shortfall when a government spends more than it earns in a given period, requiring borrowing or budget cuts.
Any individual, group, or organisation that has an interest in the decisions and outcomes of a governing body.
A person who reports illegal, unethical, or harmful activity within an organisation to the authorities or public.
The government's legal right to acquire private land for public use, provided fair compensation is paid.
The practice of making government decisions and processes open and visible to the public.
A Government of India initiative to develop cities with core infrastructure, clean environment, and technology-driven solutions for citizens.
The practice of preserving buildings, sites, and cultural artefacts of historical significance for future generations.
A funding arrangement where a government body commits its own money to match grants received from another level of government.
A detailed analysis of a proposed project's viability, including costs, benefits, risks, and alternatives.

scenes.title: The Inheritance
scenes.narrative: Your first morning as Mayor of Nagpur. The city's population has grown 40% in seven years. Traffic chokes the main arteries. Three slum settlements near the railway are without piped water. And your predecessor left a ₹280 crore fiscal gap that nobody mentioned during the election campaign. Your deputy, Nandita, slides a folder across the desk: 'You have three immediate priorities competing for the same limited budget. You need to decide where to start.'
scenes.image_prompt: New Indian mayor behind a large mayoral desk, receiving a budget briefing, city visible through floor-to-ceiling windows, morning light, serious and determined expression, photorealistic
scenes.coaching_moment: The first decisions of a new leader set the culture, the priorities, and the expectations. Choose what you prioritise based on values — not just what is easiest.
scenes.reflection_prompt: If you could only fix one thing in your city today, what would it tell people about your values?

choices.label: Prioritise the water supply for the three slum settlements — basic rights come first
choices.description: Equity-led governance. The most vulnerable first.

choices.label: Address the fiscal deficit first — you cannot govern without financial stability
choices.description: Structural fix before visible wins. Less popular but responsible.
choices.counterfactual_feedback: You optimize for strategic thinking, but at this moment the scene asks you to lead with ethical reasoning. Structural fix before visible wins. Less popular but responsible.

choices.label: Commission an independent audit of all three priorities and go public with the findings
choices.description: Transparent and accountable. Earns trust before earns wins.
choices.counterfactual_feedback: You optimize for strategic thinking, but at this moment the scene asks you to lead with ethical reasoning. Transparent and accountable. Earns trust before earns wins.

expert_pick.reason: Best aligns with the dimensions this scene rewards: ethical reasoning.

scenes.title: The Lobbyist's Lunch
scenes.narrative: Over lunch, a senior representative from Kalyan Constructions — one of the largest political donors in the state — presents you with a proposal: a 14-storey commercial complex on unused municipal land near the river. They promise 1,800 permanent jobs. The catch: the land is designated as a public green space in the development plan, and the river zone is legally protected from construction. The representative smiles: 'The last mayor was very practical about these things.'
scenes.image_prompt: Indian mayor in a high-end restaurant facing a lobbyist presenting a development proposal, city skyline visible through restaurant windows, the mayor looks composed but wary, photorealistic
scenes.coaching_moment: Political pressure to bend rules is normal in governance. How you respond to the first test sets a precedent for every test that follows.

choices.label: Decline politely but firmly — protected land is protected land, regardless of donation history
choices.description: Set the ethical floor on day one. They will test it again.
choices.counterfactual_feedback: You leaned into doing the right thing — but rightness without legitimacy is just righteousness — the people affected need a say in what right means. Set the ethical floor on day one. They will test it again.

choices.label: Ask the legal team to review if there is a compliant way to proceed with the development
choices.description: Due diligence before a full no. But appearances matter too.
choices.counterfactual_feedback: You optimize for strategic thinking, but at this moment the scene asks you to lead with ethical reasoning. Due diligence before a full no. But appearances matter too.

choices.label: Counter-propose an alternative site on non-protected land with expedited approval
choices.description: Problem-solve around the ethical constraint. Practical and principled.

expert_pick.reason: Best aligns with the dimensions this scene rewards: ethical reasoning.

scenes.title: The Town Hall
scenes.narrative: Your first public town hall is standing-room only. Three hundred residents show up. A software engineer from Dharampeth asks about potholed roads. A mother from the settlement near the railway talks about her child who got sick from bad water. A businessman complains about slow permits. And a young activist from the university holds up a sign: 'Where is the river cleanup plan?' Each voice represents thousands. You have ten minutes to speak — and you cannot promise everything.
scenes.image_prompt: Indian mayor at a town hall podium facing a packed and diverse crowd of citizens, some holding signs, respectful but intense atmosphere, community hall setting, photorealistic
scenes.coaching_moment: A leader who overpromises to manage a crowd creates distrust faster than a leader who speaks honestly about constraints. The public can absorb hard truth — what it cannot absorb is deception.

choices.label: Be completely honest about the fiscal reality — name the constraints before making any promises
choices.description: Trust-first leadership. Respect citizens enough to tell them the truth.

choices.label: Address the water crisis directly and make a 90-day public commitment
choices.description: Specific, measurable, accountable. High risk if you miss it.
choices.counterfactual_feedback: You optimize for risk tolerance, but at this moment the scene asks you to lead with ethical reasoning. Specific, measurable, accountable. High risk if you miss it.

expert_pick.reason: Best aligns with the dimensions this scene rewards: ethical reasoning.

scenes.title: The Leak
scenes.narrative: A whistleblower — an engineer from the municipal water authority — sends you confidential documents late on a Wednesday night. They show that AroChem Industrial Park has been illegally discharging chemical effluent into the Kanhan River for 18 months. The same river feeds two of the water treatment plants serving 600,000 residents. The company has significant political connections and employs 3,200 people. Your legal advisor says: 'If we act fast, we can stop further contamination. If we go public now, there will be panic.'
scenes.image_prompt: Indian mayor in a late-night office meeting with advisors, leaked documents on the desk, urgent and troubled atmosphere, city lights visible outside at night, photorealistic
scenes.coaching_moment: When institutional cover-up and public safety conflict, clarity about your core obligation as a public servant is the only compass that does not fail you.

choices.label: Issue an immediate public health advisory and order an independent water test
choices.description: Public safety first. Transparency even when it creates panic.

choices.label: Quietly order emergency water testing and shut down the discharge before going public
choices.description: Fix first, communicate second. Avoid panic while protecting safety.
choices.counterfactual_feedback: You optimize for strategic thinking, but at this moment the scene asks you to lead with ethical reasoning. Fix first, communicate second. Avoid panic while protecting safety.

choices.label: Contact the company CEO first — give them 24 hours to self-report or face enforcement
choices.description: Give the company a face-saving exit while protecting public safety.
choices.counterfactual_feedback: You optimize for adaptability, but at this moment the scene asks you to lead with ethical reasoning. Give the company a face-saving exit while protecting public safety.

expert_pick.reason: Best aligns with the dimensions this scene rewards: ethical reasoning.

scenes.title: The Pressure Campaign
scenes.narrative: AroChem's lawyer delivers a letter threatening a ₹400 crore lawsuit against the municipal corporation if you proceed with enforcement. Three state-level politicians — all from your own party — call you within the same afternoon. One says outright: 'Back off. We can't afford to lose those 3,200 votes before the assembly election.' Your Deputy Nandita sits across from you, stone-faced: 'Whatever you decide, I will back you. But decide clearly and decide fast.'
scenes.image_prompt: Indian mayor fielding multiple calls and a legal letter, looking calm under immense political pressure, advisors in the background, high-tension government office, photorealistic
scenes.coaching_moment: Political courage is not the absence of fear about consequences — it is the ability to hold your core obligation when the pressure is highest. What you do here defines what kind of leader you are.
scenes.reflection_prompt: At what cost would you compromise your ethical stand — and what does that answer reveal about your values?

choices.label: Hold firm — file enforcement action regardless of the political and legal threats
choices.description: The law exists to protect the public. Follow it regardless of cost.

choices.label: Escalate to the state environment ministry and pass the enforcement responsibility upward
choices.description: Use institutional channels. Not backing down, but not standing alone.
choices.counterfactual_feedback: You optimize for strategic thinking, but at this moment the scene asks you to lead with ethical reasoning. Use institutional channels. Not backing down, but not standing alone.

expert_pick.reason: Best aligns with the dimensions this scene rewards: ethical reasoning.

scenes.title: The Press Conference
scenes.narrative: You hold a press conference. Every major news outlet in Maharashtra is in the room. You present the water testing data, the whistleblower documents (with the source protected), and a detailed remediation plan with a 30-day public timeline. Halfway through, a journalist asks: 'Mayor, three members of your own party have called for your resignation. Do you have a response?' The room is absolutely silent.
scenes.image_prompt: Indian mayor standing at a press conference podium, cameras flashing, a tense question from a journalist, composed but serious expression, full press room, photorealistic
scenes.coaching_moment: The moments that define your integrity are not when everyone is watching and supportive — they are when the cost of the right choice is highest.

choices.label: 'My job is to protect the citizens of this city. If that costs me my seat, I can live with that'
choices.description: Moral clarity on record. The defining statement.

choices.label: Deflect the political question and refocus on the public health remediation plan
choices.description: Stay on substance. Don't let politics distract from the issue.
choices.counterfactual_feedback: You optimize for strategic thinking, but at this moment the scene asks you to lead with ethical reasoning. Stay on substance. Don't let politics distract from the issue.

expert_pick.reason: Best aligns with the dimensions this scene rewards: ethical reasoning.

scenes.title: The Redevelopment Vote
scenes.narrative: Three months after the water crisis. The river is being remediated. AroChem is under legal investigation. And now the biggest vote of your term is in front of the municipal council: a proposal to redevelop the Kalamna wholesale market area into a mixed-use district with affordable housing, green space, and a new transit hub. It requires relocating 4,000 vendors who have operated there for 30 years. The plan is good for the city's future — but deeply disruptive for thousands of families today.
scenes.image_prompt: City council chamber with a detailed urban redevelopment map on a large screen, mayor presenting to councillors, development renderings showing before and after, photorealistic
scenes.coaching_moment: Urban development always creates winners and losers. Ethical governance requires ensuring that those who lose out are not simply the ones with the least political power.

choices.label: Proceed with the plan but mandate a full vendor relocation package before any demolition begins
choices.description: Progress with protection. Take longer, do it right.
choices.counterfactual_feedback: You optimize for empathy, but at this moment the scene asks you to lead with ethical reasoning. Progress with protection. Take longer, do it right.

choices.label: Call for a 60-day community consultation before any council vote
choices.description: Democratic and thorough. Earns legitimacy even if it slows progress.

choices.label: Push for the vote now — the city's long-term future cannot be held hostage by short-term disruption
choices.description: Decisive but risks losing trust of the affected community.
choices.counterfactual_feedback: You optimize for strategic thinking, but at this moment the scene asks you to lead with ethical reasoning. Decisive but risks losing trust of the affected community.

expert_pick.reason: Best aligns with the dimensions this scene rewards: ethical reasoning.

scenes.title: The Night Before the Vote
scenes.narrative: The night before the council vote, you receive two things: a poll showing your approval rating has climbed to 67% — the highest of any Nagpur mayor in a decade — and a personal letter from Rekha Bai, a vegetable vendor who has operated at the Kalamna market for 31 years. She writes: 'Mayor sahib, I have nowhere to go. My husband is sick. This market is our home. Please do not forget people like me when you make big decisions for the big city.' You read it twice.
scenes.image_prompt: Indian mayor reading a handwritten letter alone at a desk late at night, official papers and approval rating report nearby, moved and reflective, warm lamp light, photorealistic
scenes.coaching_moment: Governance metrics and human stories must inform each other. Approval ratings measure popularity; letters like Rekha Bai's measure your actual impact on real lives.
scenes.reflection_prompt: How do you hold both the big picture and the individual human cost in the same decision?

choices.label: Respond to Rekha Bai personally and assign a senior officer to follow her case individually
choices.description: Small act of care that honours the scale of the disruption.

choices.label: Use her letter to strengthen the relocation package in the final proposal
choices.description: Turn individual pain into systemic protection for all 4,000 families.
choices.counterfactual_feedback: You optimize for strategic thinking, but at this moment the scene asks you to lead with ethical reasoning. Turn individual pain into systemic protection for all 4,000 families.

expert_pick.reason: Best aligns with the dimensions this scene rewards: ethical reasoning.

scenes.title: The Legacy Vote
scenes.narrative: The council votes 11 to 4 in favour of the redevelopment with your enhanced relocation package. You stand outside the council building afterward. Nandita says: 'Six months ago you inherited a deficit and a cover-up. Today you have a cleaned river, a 67% approval rating, and a city development plan that actually protects people. That is not nothing.' You look at the city spread out below the council steps, and you feel the weight of it — the real weight — for the first time.
scenes.image_prompt: Indian mayor standing outside the city council building at dusk, city lights beginning to appear, thoughtful and quietly proud expression, photorealistic
scenes.coaching_moment: Leadership is not a title or a term — it is the accumulated weight of every decision you made when the right thing was also the harder thing.

choices.label: 'The city taught me more about ethics than any class ever could'
choices.description: Wisdom earned in the hardest school — real governance.
choices.counterfactual_feedback: You leaned into doing the right thing — but rightness without legitimacy is just righteousness — the people affected need a say in what right means. Wisdom earned in the hardest school — real governance.

choices.label: 'Every decision cost more than I expected — and meant more than I expected too'
choices.description: Honest reckoning with the true weight of public responsibility.

expert_pick.reason: Best aligns with the dimensions this scene rewards: ethical reasoning.

scenes.title: The Metro Proposal
scenes.narrative: Three months after the redevelopment vote, a central government delegation arrives with a proposal: Nagpur has been shortlisted for a ₹4,200 crore metro extension under the Smart Cities Mission. The catch — the city must commit ₹800 crore in matching funds within 60 days, and the proposed route runs through two heritage neighbourhoods that have resisted modernisation for decades. Nandita hands you the feasibility report: 'This could define the next 20 years of this city. Or it could be the debt that drowns it.'
scenes.image_prompt: Indian mayor reviewing a massive metro infrastructure proposal with government officials, detailed transit maps on the table, modern government office, serious deliberation, photorealistic
scenes.coaching_moment: Transformative infrastructure decisions require balancing long-term vision with immediate community impact — and being honest about who bears the cost of progress.

choices.label: Commission an independent cost-benefit analysis before committing any funds
choices.description: Evidence before enthusiasm. Protect the city from impulse.
choices.counterfactual_feedback: You optimize for strategic thinking, but at this moment the scene asks you to lead with ethical reasoning. Evidence before enthusiasm. Protect the city from impulse.

choices.label: Accept the proposal but negotiate for heritage corridor protections in the route design
choices.description: Say yes to progress while drawing a line on what cannot be sacrificed.

choices.label: Reject the proposal — the city cannot afford ₹800 crore in debt right now
choices.description: Fiscal discipline over ambition. Unpopular but responsible.
choices.counterfactual_feedback: You optimize for risk tolerance, but at this moment the scene asks you to lead with ethical reasoning. Fiscal discipline over ambition. Unpopular but responsible.

expert_pick.reason: Best aligns with the dimensions this scene rewards: ethical reasoning.

scenes.title: The Heritage Protests
scenes.narrative: Residents of the Sitabuldi heritage neighbourhood have organised a sit-in protest against the proposed metro route. Among them is 78-year-old Professor Kulkarni, a retired history professor whose family home — a 140-year-old wada — sits directly on the proposed alignment. He tells a journalist: 'A city that forgets its past does not deserve a future.' Meanwhile, the central government liaison warns you that any delay could cost Nagpur its slot in the programme.
scenes.image_prompt: Elderly Indian professor leading a heritage neighbourhood protest against metro construction, historic buildings in background, passionate but peaceful demonstration, photorealistic
scenes.coaching_moment: Heritage and progress are not always enemies — but when they collide, the leader who listens to both sides before choosing earns trust from everyone.
scenes.reflection_prompt: What is the difference between preserving heritage and resisting change?

choices.label: Meet Professor Kulkarni personally and explore a route modification that saves the wada
choices.description: Honour the individual voice. Find the creative solution.
choices.counterfactual_feedback: You optimize for empathy, but at this moment the scene asks you to lead with ethical reasoning. Honour the individual voice. Find the creative solution.

choices.label: Hold a public hearing where both heritage advocates and metro supporters present their case
choices.description: Democratic process. Let the community decide its own trade-offs.

expert_pick.reason: Best aligns with the dimensions this scene rewards: ethical reasoning.

scenes.title: The Midnight Compromise
scenes.narrative: After three weeks of heated debate, you broker a compromise at a midnight council session: the metro route will be modified to tunnel under the heritage district — costlier by ₹120 crore, but preserving the neighbourhood above. Professor Kulkarni shakes your hand outside the council building. 'You listened,' he says simply. The central government approves the modified plan. Nandita looks at you: 'That was the most expensive handshake in Nagpur's history. And probably the most important.'
scenes.image_prompt: Indian mayor and elderly professor shaking hands outside a council building at night, city lights behind them, relief and mutual respect visible, photorealistic
scenes.coaching_moment: The best infrastructure decisions are not the cheapest or fastest — they are the ones that carry the community's trust forward into the future.

choices.label: Use this model — community-first infrastructure — as the template for all future projects
choices.description: Institutionalise what worked. Turn a win into a system.

choices.label: Acknowledge the cost honestly — this approach is not always sustainable at scale
choices.description: Realism over idealism. The city needs honesty about trade-offs.
choices.counterfactual_feedback: You optimize for resilience, but at this moment the scene asks you to lead with ethical reasoning. Realism over idealism. The city needs honesty about trade-offs.

expert_pick.reason: Best aligns with the dimensions this scene rewards: ethical reasoning.

scenes.title: The Succession Question
scenes.narrative: With six months left in your term, the party leadership approaches you about endorsing a successor. They want you to back Rajesh Patil, a loyal party insider with deep connections but no track record on the reforms you have championed. The alternative is Nandita — your deputy, who has earned the respect of every department head in the city — but she belongs to a different political faction and endorsing her could cost you your party standing.
scenes.image_prompt: Indian mayor in a private meeting with party leaders, weighing a political succession decision, serious faces around a conference table, photorealistic
scenes.coaching_moment: True leadership is measured not by what you built during your term, but by what survives after you leave. The successor you choose is your final policy decision.

choices.label: Endorse Nandita publicly — competence and continuity matter more than party loyalty
choices.description: Put the city first. Accept the political cost.
choices.counterfactual_feedback: You leaned into doing the right thing — but rightness without legitimacy is just righteousness — the people affected need a say in what right means. Put the city first. Accept the political cost.

choices.label: Stay neutral and let the democratic process decide — your endorsement should not be a kingmaker tool
choices.description: Respect democracy. Step back and let the people choose.

choices.label: Endorse Rajesh but negotiate binding commitments on your reform agenda as a condition
choices.description: Party loyalty with policy safeguards. A pragmatic compromise.
choices.counterfactual_feedback: You optimize for strategic thinking, but at this moment the scene asks you to lead with ethical reasoning. Party loyalty with policy safeguards. A pragmatic compromise.

expert_pick.reason: Best aligns with the dimensions this scene rewards: ethical reasoning.

scenes.title: The Time Capsule
scenes.narrative: A local school invites you to a special ceremony: students from the municipal school near the old Kalamna market have created a 'time capsule' project, collecting letters from residents about what they want Nagpur to look like in 2050. A 12-year-old girl named Aarti stands up and reads her letter: 'Dear future Nagpur, I hope you still have the mango trees near Ambazari Lake. I hope the air is clean enough to play cricket outside. And I hope the people who make decisions about our city still care about people like us.' The audience is silent. You feel the weight of her words settle on your shoulders.
scenes.image_prompt: Indian schoolgirl reading a letter at a public ceremony with the mayor watching emotionally, time capsule project visible, community gathering, warm lighting, photorealistic
scenes.coaching_moment: The children who inherit your decisions cannot vote, lobby, or protest. Governing with their future in mind is the deepest form of ethical leadership.
scenes.reflection_prompt: What would a 12-year-old version of yourself want from the leaders making decisions about your city today?

choices.label: Launch a 'Nagpur 2050' citizen planning initiative before your term ends — make long-term thinking official policy
choices.description: Institutionalise the future. Make it harder for the next mayor to forget.

choices.label: Respond to Aarti personally and commit to planting 10,000 trees in the final months of your term
choices.description: A tangible, visible act that honours her words with action.
choices.counterfactual_feedback: You optimize for empathy, but at this moment the scene asks you to lead with ethical reasoning. A tangible, visible act that honours her words with action.

expert_pick.reason: Best aligns with the dimensions this scene rewards: ethical reasoning.

scenes.title: The Last Day
scenes.narrative: Your last day as Mayor. You walk through the corridors of the municipal building one final time. The river is cleaner than it has been in 20 years. The metro construction has begun without displacing a single heritage home. The vendors from Kalamna are thriving in their new market spaces. And Rekha Bai — the vegetable vendor who wrote you that letter — sent you a box of fresh vegetables with a note: 'Thank you for remembering us, Mayor sahib.' You stand at the window of the office you inherited with a ₹280 crore deficit and a cover-up. You leave it with a city that, for all its problems, believes its government cares. That is not nothing. That is everything.
scenes.image_prompt: Indian mayor standing at the window of the mayoral office on the last day, city panorama visible, box of vegetables with a handwritten note on the desk, bittersweet and proud expression, golden hour light, photorealistic
scenes.coaching_moment: Leadership that leaves behind stronger institutions, cleaner systems, and citizens who trust their government — that is the only legacy that matters.

choices.label: 'I came in wanting to change the city. The city changed me instead — and I am grateful for every scar'
choices.description: The humility of a leader transformed by the weight of real responsibility.
choices.ending_message: You governed with conscience, fought corruption, preserved heritage, delivered infrastructure, and left behind a city that trusts its institutions more than when you arrived. Rekha Bai's vegetables on your desk say more about your legacy than any approval rating ever could. The city will remember the mayor who remembered the people.
choices.counterfactual_feedback: You leaned into doing the right thing — but rightness without legitimacy is just righteousness — the people affected need a say in what right means. The humility of a leader transformed by the weight of real responsibility.

choices.label: 'The hardest thing about this job was not the decisions — it was living with the ones I could not undo'
choices.description: Honest reckoning with the permanence of governance decisions.
choices.ending_message: Not every decision was perfect. Some trade-offs haunt you still. But a leader who carries the weight of their choices honestly — who does not pretend governance was easy or costless — leaves behind something more valuable than a clean record: they leave behind the truth. And truth is the foundation every future leader needs.

expert_pick.reason: Best aligns with the dimensions this scene rewards: ethical reasoning.

coaching_moment: Governance is the art of making decisions under uncertainty with incomplete information — knowing that inaction is itself a choice with consequences.
cultural_context: India's rapid urbanisation — with 600 million people expected in cities by 2031 — creates exactly the governance challenges this game explores. Urban management trade-offs between infrastructure, public health, and political accountability are central to India's development agenda.

hallmarks: Reads the room before reading the budget — listens to citizens before optimizing the spreadsheet
Names the trade-off out loud instead of pretending all priorities can be funded
Distinguishes between what is urgent (slums need water now) and what is foundational (fiscal stability)
Brings opponents into the process early instead of presenting decisions as fait accompli
Treats one neighborhood's loss as the city's loss — refuses zero-sum politics
Optimizes for the next press cycle rather than the next election cycle
Treats the budget as untouchable when ethics demand the harder spend
Confuses popularity in polls with legitimacy with citizens
Defers to bureaucracy when leadership is needed — and to instinct when data is needed
Plays favorites and calls it pragmatism

challenge_persona_ladder: a senior bureaucrat in your administration, polite but pointed, who has watched many mayors flame out
the leader of the opposition in council, quoting your last reply in public, looking for the exact phrase to clip
an angry citizen at a town hall who is directly affected by your decision and is no longer interested in process

reflection_prompt: Looking back at the choices you made, which one felt hardest and why? What would you do differently if you replayed?
